title: Runtime DB and Unity Export Map
purpose: Data-only seed map that defines how approved LLMGameCreator artifacts should be compiled into runtime databases, save overlays, Unity IR, asset indexes and Unity runtime shell inputs.
principles: Unity runtime consumes compiled runtime data, Unity IR, asset indexes and save overlays; it does not consume unbounded loose generated JSON files at runtime.
GamePackage and approved artifacts remain authoring/source data; runtime.db is a compiled read-optimized product.
Mutable player/world state is stored separately from immutable compiled content, usually in save.db or an equivalent save overlay.
Lua and LLM workflows may propose runtime DB build plans or Unity IR, but C# build/export services own compilation, indexing, validation, migration and export.
Unity adapters bind data to existing runtime shell capabilities; they should not require custom generated C# for every game mechanic.
Asset generation requests, including adult/NSFW image/audio/future animation requests when enabled, remain tagged artifacts and must pass export/platform filters before becoming asset references.
The runtime database is an optimization and deployment artifact, not the only source of truth for design history or generation decisions.
Every table, index, Unity IR group and asset binding must be traceable back to approved source artifacts and contract ids.

compiled_outputs.purpose: Read-optimized compiled game content, semantic data, text packs, rules, formulas, asset references and Unity binding data.
Schema/migration description for mutable player saves.
Player/world state, NPC memory, quest progress, inventory state, chunk deltas and event log.
Asset ids, generated/imported asset references, variants, tags, platform filters and Unity addressable/prefab bindings.
Unity-facing scene, UI, camera, input, prefab, VFX, audio and runtime shell binding descriptors.
Build version, source artifact hashes, schema versions, contract ids, export target and validation summary.

runtime_db_table_groups.purpose: World structure, maps, chunks, prototypes and placed entities.
Items, equipment, paper-doll/grid inventory and loot.
Dialogue graphs, text realization, localized variants and morphology lookup.
Data-driven mechanics, formulas, abilities, combat and status effects.
Faction, reputation, quest and narrative progression data.
Asset and Unity runtime shell binding data.
Optional adult/NSFW, horror/gore and other tagged content overlays with export-aware filters.

save_db_table_groups.purpose: Narrative, social and dialogue memory state.

unity_ir_groups.purpose: Selects Unity runtime shell mode and core services.
Maps content ids to Unity prefabs/addressables without generating gameplay code.
Data-driven UI layout and binding hints for Unity runtime UI.
Audio, VFX and future animation hooks tied to approved content and runtime events.

performance_rules: Use many small authoring files if convenient, but compile them into indexed runtime data before Unity player runtime.
Prefer stable ids and indexed lookups over scanning JSON arrays at runtime.
Keep heavy generation, normalization and morphology compilation out of the final player runtime.
Use chunk/region/entity indexes for large or infinite worlds.
Use content tags and export filters for optional overlays instead of duplicating entire data sets.
Keep runtime.db read-only during play; write mutable data into save.db/save overlays.
Record source artifact hashes so compiled data can be invalidated and rebuilt deterministically.
must_not: Do not make Unity runtime scan arbitrary generator-library Lua files.
Do not make Unity runtime trust raw LLM output.
Do not mix immutable compiled content and mutable player save state without a clear partition.
Do not silently enable adult/NSFW overlays during export.
Do not require custom generated C# for every small feature when a data-driven Unity adapter can consume IR.
Do not treat runtime.db as the only source of truth for authoring or design history.
